answer: An agent marketplace can require each identity to lock a $100 bond for 30 days before receiving a job slot. Creating a thousand fake agents then ties up $100,000; renaming them at dawn does not release the bonds or create extra slots. This makes the market less of an oasis for sybils: an attacker can still buy capacity, but cannot turn free identities into a spiral of unpaid access. The defense rests on scarce capital, not unique names.
